taste.name: Annotated link index instead of a navigation bar
taste.trigger: When the designers had to route first-time visitors to pricing, features, migration stories, reliability and developer docs
taste.decision: Chose seven bold underlined links in the hero column, each followed by an em-dash gloss in plain words ('Pricing & sign up - A free plan + paid upgrades'), over a horizontal nav bar with Product / Solutions / Resources dropdowns
taste.reason: Because a visitor who does not know the vendor's vocabulary can only choose a destination when told what is behind it; a gloss answers 'what is this?' before the click instead of after
evidence: header holds only 3 items: 'Have an account? Sign in', logo, 'Want an account? Sign up free'
no nav menu at 1440; 390 collapses to hamburger
footer repeats the pattern as a 36-chip link wall of sentence-titled pages

taste.name: A signed founder letter carries the pitch
taste.trigger: When the page had to explain why the product exists right after the hero
taste.decision: Chose a ~660px-wide letter in 19.15px body on a stacked, slightly rotated paper card, opening 'Hey there- Tell me if this sounds about right.' and closing with a handwritten signature, headshot and the CEO's real email, over a three-icon benefit row or feature grid
taste.reason: Because a reader recognizes their own problem faster in second-person prose than in feature labels, and a named person with a reachable address reads as accountable in a way an icon grid cannot
evidence: section 2 has no headline, only 'Hey there-'
3 offset paper layers behind the card

taste.name: One family, hierarchy by weight jump
taste.trigger: When the page needed loud section headings and calm supporting copy without a display typeface
taste.decision: Chose Graphik alone, pairing 800-weight headings at -1.11px tracking with 400-weight subheads only 1.375x smaller, over a display/serif + sans pairing
taste.reason: Because the 800-to-400 contrast reads as 'headline, then plain explanation' at a glance, and a single family keeps the conversational letter and the bold claims in the same voice

taste.name: Flat square panels; blue fill reserved for the two commitments
taste.trigger: When separating ten stacked sections on a long dark page
taste.decision: Chose 0px-radius #1B2930 panels on a #0B151B frame, separated by ~184px gaps and a wavy hand-drawn line with the logo glyph, with filled #117AF3 used only on 'Sign up free' and 'Subscribe', over rounded gradient cards and a colored CTA in every section
taste.reason: Because when only two controls are filled, the reader never wonders which button is the real one; every other ask is an underlined link or a play button that costs nothing to try
evidence: section panels, buttons, email input all 0px radius
panel area 28.5% + 15.7%; blue fill ~1.2% of area
links #68A8F4 underlined, video asks as white 0px-radius chips with a play triangle
divider: ~400px wavy line + 30px mountain glyph centered between panels
